title: Evaluation package
description: Immutable, self-describing evaluation package compiled by B3 from a published question version and consumed by B2's runner core. This is the highest-risk coupling point in the system: B2 must be able to execute a package without understanding the question's semantics, and adding a question type must not require changing the runner core (RQ-B-3-40/50/60). The package carries reference answers, hidden test cases and expected outputs, so it is service-to-service only and must never be reachable from a student-facing surface.

question_version_id.description: The immutable question version this package was compiled from.

package_digest.description: Canonical digest of the package content. Bound into every evaluation and reported in the result so a score can be traced to the exact package that produced it.

language.description: Graded language (RQ-B-0-10). B2 selects interpreter, static checker and sandbox policy from this value; a submission in a different language is rejected with 422.

execution.description: Explicit declaration of how this package's cases are produced from an execution. Absence means the legacy per-case mode (one sandbox execution per case), so packages compiled before this field existed stay valid and byte-identical. Behaviour is never selected by a title, tag, path or magic string: it is this field or nothing.

segment_delimiter.description: Required when cases are split out of one run. The marker must occupy an entire output line by itself and must not be a prefix/suffix of other output. Missing, extra or misordered segments fail every segment case; a segment is never re-assigned to another case.

email.description: email_delivery only: what the received message must satisfy. The receipt itself is recorded by the real IMAP intake, not by this package.

ssh.description: ssh_session only: the real practice service started inside the isolated sandbox. The password is protected content and must never appear in a public DTO, event or log.

host.description: The question requires logging in to localhost; any other address would leave the isolated network namespace.

adapter.description: How the submission is exercised. One shared structure for all three frameworks.

kind.description: stdin = command line input (RQ-B-3-40); file = reads test data from files (RQ-B-3-50); callable = imported and invoked (RQ-B-3-60).

args.description: Argument vector passed as an array. It is never interpolated into a shell string, so arguments containing shell metacharacters stay literal.

comparison.description: Comparison policy declared by the question author. Student code must not be able to influence it: the runner takes it from the package, never from anything the submission provides.

files.description: Fixtures copied into the sandbox workspace before execution (relevant for kind=file). Paths are workspace-relative; absolute paths and '..' are rejected.

callable.description: Entry point resolved inside the workspace (relevant for kind=callable). Loading from arbitrary absolute paths or over the network is forbidden.

tests.description: Hidden test cases. Never present in a public DTO, an event, a log line or a student-visible export.

ordinal.description: Stable execution order; results are reported per ordinal so evidence can be compared across runs.

visible_to_student.description: Whether the student may see this case's input and expected output. Defaults to false; hidden cases must stay hidden.

segment.description: single_run only: which delimiter-separated stdout segment this case compares. The declared segment values must be exactly 0..N-1, one per segment case; a case is only ever compared against its own segment.

file_checks.description: Assertions the evaluator makes directly on final workspace files after the run (never on the student's stdout). Used by the vi part of a file-editing question: the edited bytes and the permission bits are both checked, so printing a fabricated `stat` line cannot pass.

content_sha256.description: PROTECTED. Digest of the expected final bytes; null means content is not asserted.

mode.description: Expected permission bits as canonical four-digit octal text, e.g. "0744". Null means permissions are not asserted; the three-digit form is refused because the evaluator formats actual bits in the same canonical form.

ssh_check.description: ssh_session only: which real server-side fact this case judges. Exactly one of each value may appear in a package.

email_check.description: email_delivery only: which fact about the actually received message this case judges. Exactly one of each value may appear in a package.

security_policy.description: Sandbox policy applied to every case in this package. The constants encode non-negotiable guarantees from ADR-0004: no network, read-only root, non-root user. Numeric limits are enforced by cgroup v2 and seccomp.

network.description: Network access is always denied. A package cannot opt out.

read_only_root.description: The root filesystem is always read-only. A package cannot opt out.

allow_root.description: Graded code never runs as root. A package cannot opt out.

max_memory_bytes.description: Bounded by the resource ledger: a single concurrent sandbox job is capped at 96 MB.

max_files.description: Submission file count limit declared per question (RQ-B-2-10).

max_total_bytes.description: Submission total size limit declared per question.

created_at.description: When this package's content was fixed. For a published version it equals `published_at` (the package is an immutable artifact); for a draft (CHG-0028) it is the draft content's own timestamp, because a draft has no `published_at` and its package is a snapshot of current content rather than a frozen one. Excluded from `package_digest`, so it never affects the digest.
